source_text: Asserta examinis sui libra iam tunc opinionem vestram in his, qui similia arbitrabantur, accusat. Et dixistis: Quid est quod non accepit iniquitatem patris sui filius? Quoniam anima - inquit - quae peccat, ipsa morietur; filius autem non accipit iniustitiam patris sui neque pater accipit iniustitiam filii sui; iustitia iusti super ipsum erit et iniquitas iniqui super ipsum erit [n63] . Quis nostrum hinc cum tanta diligentia umquam disputare potuisset, cum quanta Deus per os Prophetae sui dividendo, comparando repetendoque disseruit?
pass_a_gloss: The asserted scale of his examination already then accuses your opinion in those who were judging similar things. And you have said: What is it that the son has not received his father's iniquity? Since the soul, he says, which sins, itself will die; but the son does not receive the injustice of his father nor the father the injustice of his son; the justice of the just will be upon himself and the iniquity of the iniquitous upon himself. Which of us could ever have disputed from here with as much diligence as God through the mouth of his Prophet has discoursed by dividing, comparing, and repeating?

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: Having established the balanced scales of his judgment, he was already condemning your opinion in people who thought similarly. ‘You have said: Why has the son not borne his father’s iniquity? Because,’ he says, ‘the soul that sins shall itself die. The son does not bear his father’s injustice, nor does the father bear his son’s injustice. The just person’s justice shall rest on himself, and the wicked person’s wickedness shall rest on himself’ (Ezekiel 18:19–20). Which of us could ever have discussed this with as much care as God did through his prophet’s mouth, distinguishing, comparing, and repeating the points?

choices.why: Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
